Pianist, composer and educator Norman Simmons was born in Chicago on October 6, 1929. He is well known as an arranger, recording artist and accompanist, having served in this role with Dakota Staton, Carmen McRae and Joe Williams. Norman currently directs Milljac Productions and an ensemble devoted to the music of Duke Ellington.
Norman was interviewed in Clinton, New York on September 27, 2007 by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.

My name is Monk Rowe and I’m director of the Jazz Archive here at Hamilton College. I’m very pleased to have Norman Simmons here for a second interview and have you at the college for some musical events. Welcome.
Thank you very much. It’s a pleasure to be here again.
